SkillPointsLevel5.Name: Skill Points for Level 5 Skills
SkillPointsLevel5.Hint: Skill points required to reach level 1 of a 5-level skill. The requirement doubles for each subsequent level.

SkillPointsLevel10.Name: Skill Points for Level 10 Skills
SkillPointsLevel10.Hint: Skill points required to reach level 1 of a 10-level skill. The requirement increases by this amount for each subsequent level.

CarryWeightFormula.Name: Max Carry Weight Formula
CarryWeightFormula.Hint: Base max carry weight, before size-category scaling (Tiny 25%, Small 75%, Medium 100%, Large 150%, Huge 300%, Gigantic 1000%, Titanic unlimited). A real roll formula - reference attributes as @attributes.str.value or @attributes.str.mod, skill levels as @skills.<key> (e.g. @skills.axe), and character level as @lvl.

DurabilityEnabled.Name: Enable Durability
DurabilityEnabled.Hint: Whether Weapon/Armor/Item Durability (see the Materials and Models settings) is tracked, calculated, and shown at all. Off by default.

GeneralSettings.Name: General Settings
GeneralSettings.Hint: Skill point costs for Level 10/Level 5 skills, the max carry weight formula, and whether Durability is enabled.
GeneralSettings.Label: Configure General Settings

Materials.Name: Materials
Materials.Hint: Materials selectable on Items/Armor/Weapons. Material Bonus and Mana Capacity may each be a number, or "?" to let each item using this material set its own value instead.
Materials.Label: Configure Materials

Models.Name: Models
Models.Hint: Weapon Models (by weapon type) and Armor Models (Light Armor, Heavy Armor, Shield) selectable on Weapons/Armor.
Models.Label: Configure Models

StatusEffects.Name: Status Effects
StatusEffects.Hint: Status effects selectable/toggleable on tokens and actors. Predefined ones (Exhaustion, Dazed, the four Poisoning severities) carry their own automated mechanics and can't be removed, only re-named/re-iconned/re-described; custom ones you add are flavor-only.
StatusEffects.Label: Configure Status Effects

TrainingMethods.Name: Training Methods
TrainingMethods.Hint: Training methods Characters can use (via the sheet header's Training button) to generate pending FP for a main skill and any number of secondary skills, per hour spent training.
TrainingMethods.Label: Configure Training Methods

CombatStyles.Name: Combat Styles
CombatStyles.Hint: The named Kampfstile (combat/technique styles) Technique items can belong to - see the Technique item sheet's own Style field.
CombatStyles.Label: Configure Combat Styles

ExportImport.Name: Export/Import Settings
ExportImport.Hint: Export this world's SKSK settings (skill point costs, carry weight formula, Materials, Models, Status Effects, Training Methods, Skill Usage FP, Combat Styles, Lehren) to a JSON file, or import them from one - e.g. to back up a world's configuration or copy it to another world.
ExportImport.Label: Export/Import Settings
ExportImport.ImportHint: Importing overwrites the current values of any setting present in the chosen file. Settings not present in the file are left untouched.
ExportImport.InvalidFile: That file isn't a valid SKSK settings export.
ExportImport.NothingToImport: The chosen file contains none of this system's settings.
ExportImport.ImportConfirmContent: This will overwrite {count} setting(s) with the values from the chosen file. This cannot be undone. Continue?

SkillUsageFp.Name: Skill Usage FP
SkillUsageFp.Hint: How many FP a Character generates for using a skill (skill checks, weapon attacks, spells cast, attribute rolls, ...) - Characters only, per skill category.
SkillUsageFp.Label: Configure Skill Usage FP

Lehren.Name: Lehren
Lehren.Hint: The catalog of Lehren (Lore) available per skill - each Character freely distributes a shared pool of 5 levels across one skill's own Lehren, gated per-Lehre by its own minimum skill level.
Lehren.Label: Configure Lehren

EffectKeyReference.Name: Effect Key Reference
EffectKeyReference.Hint: A searchable list of every real Foundry Active Effect "Attribute Key" this system supports.
EffectKeyReference.Label: Browse Effect Keys

Movement.UnlockedHint: Grants access to this movement type at all, floored to a minimum speed based on the actor's size category (higher for Flying/Hovering on small creatures).

General.InspirationDieHint: Click to roll (and consume) the Inspiration die you're currently holding, once someone has granted you one.
General.NoFavoriteSkills: No favorite skills yet - star one in the Skills tab.
General.AbbreviationHint: Up to 4 letters. Usable in roll formulas as @<abbreviation>, e.g. @rage.

Longevity.ResetHint: Resets current Longevity to 100% of base Longevity (main Species including current Sub-Species multipliers).

Materials.Name: Name
Materials.VariableHint: A non-negative number, or "?" to let each item using this material set its own value

SkillFpConfig.WeaponsHint: FP generated per skill check and per weapon attack (including Martial Arts) using that skill, plus per kill - once the "Apply Damage" button brings a target to 0 Life and maximum Negative Life, or manually via the "Mark Kill" button on an actor's GM tab.
SkillFpConfig.ArmorsHint: FP generated whenever the Character is the target of a weapon or Martial Arts attack evaluation (hit or miss), for every armor-category skill currently equipped (worn body armor plus Shield, if any).
SkillFpConfig.MagicSchoolsHint: FP generated per spell level whenever a Simple or Advanced spell of that magic school is cast (e.g. a rate of 1 and a level-3 spell grants 3 FP).
SkillFpConfig.AttributeHint: FP generated whenever the corresponding attribute's own roll (not a skill check) is made - only the 8 "Unlimited X" skills apply, one per attribute.
SkillFpConfig.ResistancesHint: FP generated whenever damage of the corresponding element is taken via the "Apply Damage" button - the only skill category that's capped, though: automatic gain can never raise a Resistance past level 3 (plus any item-granted skill bonus levels); manual level changes are unaffected.
SkillFpConfig.ProductionHint: Granted via the "Production FP" header button - the player enters an already-resolved action's quality% there (plus, for Alchemy, the number of essences processed, and for Enchanting a ritual duration in hours), which scales the rate below accordingly. Enchanting additionally grants Ritualism's own "ritualHour" FP for the entered duration.
SkillFpConfig.RogueHint: Fallen's roll lets the player choose "Falle stellen" or "Falle entschärfen" when they use it (both automated); Fingerfertigkeit's roll likewise offers a choice between its base check, Schlossknacken and Taschendiebstahl (also automated). Assassination is automated too: Assassination Attack grants FP whenever a weapon/Martial Arts attack hits while Concealed (alongside Assassination's own bonus damage), Assassination Kill additionally if that same attack kills the defender.
SkillFpConfig.MagicHint: Concentration checks, used Meditation dice, any spell cast (Magic Control, Chant Shortening once Magic Control reaches level 1), Mana Capacity/Mana Regeneration's own daily settlement (on the next Anpassungspause+), Mana Core's flat per-item grant, Ritualism's hours per Ritual spell cast (at least 1 hour, even under the AP unit or a sub-60-minute casting time), Overcharge used (Shift+click a spell), Source-Bound/Ether-Bound (via the header's own "Quelle" button - Source Ability Used on "Quelle aktivieren", Source Opened on "Ätherquelle öffnen", each paying its own editable AP/Mana cost, no usage limit), and Summoning (via the header's Summoning button - Summoned Creature Level on "Beschwören", Day of Summon's Existence for every still-active slot on the next Anpassungspause+) are all automated; everything else below (enchanting hours) is not yet automated - no matching system exists yet.
SkillFpConfig.FighterHint: Regeneration dice used, combat movement, Dodge used, Reflexaktion (4+ AP spent in one turn), Adrenalin used, critical hits (incl. double crit), Brutality's bonus damage points, and Technique's own cooldown rounds (any owned Technique Item currently on cooldown, granted once per Combat round it spends there) are automated; everything else below is not yet automated.
SkillFpConfig.MiscHint: Bardic magic cast (Singing), being Concealed at the start of your own turn (Stealth), prayer via the header's Prayer button (Faith), clicks on the header's Passive Perception field (Observation), Apply Damage converting an entry into healing via the defender's own Absorption (Healer - credited to whoever caused it, scaled by the healed amount), Totem (via the header's Totem button - Totem Bond Formed on "Totem binden", Totem Used on "Totem aktivieren"), and Inspiration (via the Actions tab's own Inspiration button and the header's own Inspiration Die field - credited to whoever originally granted a die once it's actually rolled, whether by its own holder or via the granter's own Right-Click self-roll) are automated; everything else below is not yet automated - no matching system exists yet.
SkillFpConfig.SpecialHint: A landed hit (Hit Correction), a defended-against attack (Defense Correction), being at 0 Life with Negative Life left at the start of your own turn (Tenacity), any generic (non-Angriffswurf) D20 roll's critical success/double critical - skill checks, saving throws, attribute checks, and a manual Restrained escape attempt prompt for Neutral/Vorteil/Nachteil every time; Restrained's own turn-start/end check, Poison's recheck, and Concentration instead use the GM tab's Background Roll Mode preset with no dialog (Luck's own "Critical Roll"/"Double Critical Roll", credited to whoever rolled it - double only from Vorteil/Nachteil, both dice critical) - Soulforce's own "Meditation Die Used in Combat" (alongside Meditation's own FP whenever a Combat is active, but only while the GM tab's own "Soulforce: FP for Meditation in Combat" switch is also on, off by default), and Massacre's own 5 GM-tab Mass Kill buttons (20/50/150/500/1500 people killed within roughly 10 minutes, a fully manual GM judgment call - each tier's own rate depends on the actor's current Massacre skill level, independently configured per tier/level combination in the Skill Usage FP settings) - are automated; everything else below is not yet automated.
SkillFpConfig.StealthRound: FP / Round Concealed at Own Turn Start
SkillFpConfig.DailyManaSpent: FP / Accumulated Amount, on the Next Anpassungspause+
SkillFpConfig.RitualHour: FP / Hour Spent on a Ritual
SkillFpConfig.EnchantingHour: FP / Hour Spent Enchanting (not yet automated)
SkillFpConfig.ChantShorteningSpellCast: FP / Any Spell Cast (once Magic Control reaches level 1)
SkillFpConfig.ReflexActionUsed: FP / Reflexaktion (4+ AP Spent in One Turn)
SkillFpConfig.CriticalBonusDamagePoint: FP / Point of Critical Bonus Damage
SkillFpConfig.ZeroLifeRound: FP / Round at 0 Life (with Negative Life left) at Own Turn Start
SkillFpConfig.MeditationUsedInCombat: FP / Meditation Die Used in Combat

LehrenDialog.NoLehren: No Lehren defined yet for this category's skills.

LehrenDialog.PoolExceeded: Only {pool} Lehre levels can be invested per skill.

Life.MaxComputed: Automatically calculated from Classes, Constitution, Health, Tenacity and abilities - not directly editable

NegativeLife.MaxComputed: Automatically calculated from max life, minus Tenacity's multiplier unless enabled on the GM tab - not directly editable
NegativeLife.IncludeToughness: Tenacity also raises max negative life
NegativeLife.IncludeToughnessHint: Let Tenacity's multiplier also raise max negative life, instead of only max life

Mana.MaxComputed: Automatically calculated from Aura, Mana Capacity, Source Bound, Mana Core and abilities - not directly editable

ActionPoints.MaxComputed: Automatically calculated from a base of 3 plus Reflexes (up to level 3) and any effects - not directly editable

ReactionPoints.MaxComputed: Automatically calculated from max AP and Reflexes beyond level 3 - not directly editable

ArmorClass.Computed: Automatically calculated from Base AC, Constitution, worn armor/shield and any effects - not directly editable

MagicResistance.Computed: Automatically calculated from Aura, Antimagic armor/shields and any effects - not directly editable

Resource.SoulPowerHint: Soulforce's own collection resource - no maximum, spent via Breakthroughs and Path Abilities, or traded back into Soulforce FP below level 5 (see the GM tab's own "Soulforce: Enable New Mechanic" switch and this row's own trade button).
Resource.SoulPowerTradeNoRate: No Soul Power trade-in rate configured yet (see the Skill Usage FP settings).
Resource.SoulPowerTradeDescription: {name} used {amount} Soul Power to generate Soulforce.

GM.NaturalMaterialBonusHint: A flat adjustment (positive or negative) to the creature's level-based natural material bonus - a floor under worn Light/Heavy armor's own AC bonus.
GM.BaseArmorClassHint: The base of Grund-AC, before the Constitution modifier is added on top.
GM.CustomArmorClassBonusHint: A flat AC bonus (positive or negative) on top of every other AC component.
GM.CustomMagicResistanceBonusHint: A flat MR bonus (positive or negative) on top of every other MR component.
GM.CriticalHitThresholdHint: The lowest natural d20 result (on an Angriffswurf/attack roll only) that counts as a critical success. 20 by default; lowering it to e.g. 15 means 15-20 all critically hit.
GM.CriticalFailureThresholdHint: The highest natural d20 result (on an Angriffswurf/attack roll only) that counts as a critical failure. 1 by default; raising it to e.g. 5 means 1-5 all critically fail.
GM.AssassinationBonusDiceHint: Extra dice of the same size as Assassination's current skill level (see Evaluate Hit) - has no effect at level 0, which only grants a flat bonus with no dice.
GM.ManaCapacityAccumulatorHint: Real mana cost paid for spells cast since the last Anpassungs-/Genesungspause - multiplied by the Mana Capacity skillUsageFp rate and floored on the next one, then reset to 0. Not meant to be hand-edited, but visible/adjustable here if needed.
GM.ManaRegenerationAccumulatorHint: Mana actually restored (Meditation, passive regen from time/Rest) since the last Anpassungs-/Genesungspause - multiplied by the Mana Regeneration skillUsageFp rate and floored on the next one, then reset to 0. Not meant to be hand-edited, but visible/adjustable here if needed.
GM.GenericCriticalRollModeHint: Neutral/Advantage/Disadvantage preset used ONLY by fully automatic generic (non-Angriffswurf) D20 checks that trigger with no player-facing dialog - Restrained's own turn-start/end escape check, Poison's recheck, Concentration. Player-triggered generic rolls (skill checks, attribute checks, saving throws, a manual Restrained escape attempt) always prompt fresh instead and ignore this. Targetable by Active Effects.
GM.SummonSlotsBonusHint: A flat adjustment (positive or negative) to Summoning's own slot count (see the Summoning header button), on top of the Willpower modifier - applied before the multiplier below.
GM.SummonSlotsMultiplierHint: Multiplies (Willpower modifier + the bonus above) - floored, never below 0. 1 by default (no change).
GM.TotemSlotsBonusHint: A flat adjustment (positive or negative) to Totem's own slot count (see the Totem header button), on top of the Totem skill's own level - applied before the multiplier below.
GM.TotemSlotsMultiplierHint: Multiplies (Totem skill level + the bonus above) - floored, never below 0. 1 by default (no change).
GM.SoulforceMeditationCombatFpEnabled: Soulforce: FP for Meditation in Combat
GM.SoulforceMeditationCombatFpEnabledHint: Whether using a Meditation die while a Combat is active also grants Soulforce's own "Meditation Used in Combat" FP (still scaled by that trigger's own configured rate in the Skill Usage FP settings). Off by default. Targetable by Active Effects.
GM.SoulPowerResourceEnabledHint: Shows the Soul Power resource on the sidebar even before Soulforce reaches its own max level (5) - it's shown regardless once that level is reached, so this only matters earlier. Off by default. Targetable by Active Effects.
GM.SoulPowerMechanicEnabledHint: Reserved for Soul Power's own trade-in mechanic (its "Soul Power Traded" FP trigger) - not yet designed or wired up, to be tackled once every skill-usage FP trigger is fully implemented. Has no effect yet. Targetable by Active Effects.

Shift+Click to just spend a charge without granting anything (to simulate a special ability that consumes Inspiration charges). Right-Click to spend a charge and roll the die immediately for yourself.

Technique.CooldownHint: Combat rounds this Technique is unusable for after being deactivated/consumed.
Technique.DurationHint: Combat rounds this Technique stays active for once activated - only applies to Stand, and Effect Techniques targeting their own wielder.
Technique.BonusDamageHint: Added to the primed weapon/Martial Arts attack's or spell's own already-rolled damage total - independent of Dice Increase below, both may be set at once.
Technique.DiceIncreaseHint: Changes the NUMBER of the primed attack's/spell's own first damage dice term before it's rolled - independent of Bonus Damage above, both may be set at once.
Technique.HitBonusHint: Added to the primed weapon/Martial Arts attack's or spell's own Angriffswurf (to-hit roll) - independent of Bonus Damage/Dice Increase above, all three may be set at once.
Technique.ApplicableToHint: Which kind(s) of attack this Technique may be primed for/consumed by - at least one should be checked, otherwise the Technique never gets consumed.
Technique.EffectTargetHint: Whether this Technique's own effect(s) apply to its own wielder (activated like a Stand, with a duration, unconditionally - no saving throw), to whoever the next weapon/Martial Arts attack or spell cast hits (primed like Attack Bonuses, consumed by that attack/cast instead), or immediately on activation to a directly chosen target (no connection to an attack or spell at all).
Technique.EffectStatusEffectsHint: Predefined status effects (from the world's Status Effects list) this Technique applies - may be combined with its own freeform linked Active Effect (Edit Effect button below), both apply together.
Technique.StyleBonusSection: Bonus to Techniques of the Same Style (while active)
Technique.StyleBonusHint: Applied to any other Technique of the same Combat Style when it's activated/consumed while this Stand is active - everything else this Stand itself grants (AC/MR, resource points, attribute/skill boosts, ...) goes through its own linked Active Effect instead (Edit Effect button below).

Technique.OnCooldown: {name} is still on cooldown ({rounds} rounds left).

StatusEffect.Name: Name
StatusEffect.PredefinedHint: This status effect's own automated mechanics are tied to it - it can't be removed, only re-named/re-iconned/re-described.
StatusEffect.NegativeLifeOverflow: {amount} of that overflows into Negative Life
StatusEffect.StatModifiersHint: Applied automatically via a real Active Effect while this status is active on an actor, scaled by its stack count.
StatusEffect.TurnStartTicksHint: Triggers at the start of the actor's own Combat turn, scaled by its stack count. Life change is applied directly (clamped between 0 and max Life, positive heals, negative damages); Mana change is applied directly too (clamped between 0 and max Mana).
StatusEffect.BaseAttributeBonusesHint: A permanent stat increase while this status is active - affects everything, including resource maxes (Life/Mana/AP/RP/etc).
StatusEffect.SpecialAttributeBonusesHint: A semi-permanent/temporary bonus - reaches AC/MR, but never inflates a resource max.
StatusEffect.ModifierAttributeBonusesHint: Added straight to the roll modifier without touching the attribute's own value - same resource exclusion as Special.
StatusEffect.FpGainBonusesHint: Adjusts a specific skill's pending FP gain while this status is active - same positive/negative/multiplicative/forceZero rules as an item's own FP Gain Bonuses list, scaled by the current stack count.
StatusEffect.IgnoreSpecialBonusOnSave: Ignore Special Bonus on this save
StatusEffect.MovementSpellBlocked: Can't cast a Movement spell while Prone or Restrained.
StatusEffect.AttackBlocked: Can't attack while Prone or Restrained.

Exhaustion.Name: Exhaustion
Exhaustion.Description: -1 to all D20 rolls per level (up to level 9, no further malus at level 10). Reaching level 10 kills the creature outright (Life and Negative Life both set to 0).

Dazed.Name: Dazed
Dazed.Description: At the start of each of the creature's turns, drains Action Points equal to its stacks (always leaving at least 2 AP), reducing stacks by the same amount. Reduces every movement speed but Hovering by 1 per stack (floored at half); grants a malus on Strength/Dexterity/Constitution/Appearance checks equal to its stacks (capped at that attribute's own modifier + 5).

PoisonMild.Name: Mild Poisoning
PoisonMild.Description: 1d4 poison damage at the start of the poisoned creature's turn, followed by a Constitution check (DC 10) every round. A successful check cures it.

PoisonMedium.Name: Medium Poisoning
PoisonMedium.Description: 1d6 poison damage and a Constitution check (DC 13) every 3 rounds (first triggering 3 rounds after being poisoned). A successful check cures it.

PoisonSevere.Name: Severe Poisoning
PoisonSevere.Description: 1d8 poison damage and a Constitution check (DC 16) every 5 rounds (first triggering 5 rounds after being poisoned). A successful check cures it.

PoisonDeadly.Name: Deadly Poisoning
PoisonDeadly.Description: 1d10 poison damage and a Constitution check (DC 19) every 10 rounds (first triggering 10 rounds after being poisoned). A successful check cures it.

Prone.Name: Prone
Prone.Description: Can't use weapon attacks (incl. Martial Arts Attacks) or cast spells with the Movement casting method. Can still move.

Restrained.Name: Restrained
Restrained.Description: Can't move, use weapon attacks (incl. Martial Arts Attacks), or cast spells with the Movement casting method. Carries its own escape check difficulty and timing (an AP cost spendable any time, or an automatic check at the start/end of its own Combat turn) - a passed Strength check removes it entirely.

Frostbite.Name: Frostbite
Frostbite.Description: Stackable, capped at (Constitution modifier + 4) - a stack beyond the cap applies 1 Dazed stack instead. Deals flat Cold damage (2x the first Class's Life value, plus the second Class's once unlocked) at the start of each round of the creature's turn, regardless of its own stack count.

Wound.Name: Wound
Wound.Description: Can be suffered multiple times, each with its own damage value. At the start of the creature's turn, it suffers the summed damage value of every Wound.

MaxLifeDamage.Name: Max Life Damage
MaxLifeDamage.Description: Can be suffered multiple times, from different sources - each instance permanently reduces max Life by its own value (and max Negative Life too, once Tenacity's buffer is exhausted).

Cauterization.Name: Cauterization
Cauterization.Description: Comes with a value that reduces max Life (like Max Life Damage, and Negative Life too once Tenacity's buffer is exhausted). A second application doesn't stack separately - it merges into the existing value instead.

AdrenalinDamage.Name: Adrenalin Damage
AdrenalinDamage.Description: Comes with a value that reduces max Life (like Max Life Damage/Cauterization, and Negative Life too once Tenacity's buffer is exhausted), caused specifically by Adrenalin's own escalating damage. A second application doesn't stack separately - it merges into the existing value instead. Reduced (not fully healed) by Anpassungspause (Constitution modifier) or Genesungspause (whichever is higher between Character level and Constitution modifier) - Adrenalin's separate used count, which drives future rolls, resets to 0 at any qualifying Pause instead.

Charmed.Name: Charmed
Charmed.Description: This creature has been charmed by another creature. It can't attack the source of this status effect, nor target it with negative spells or other negative effects. The source of this status effect has advantage on all rolls resulting from a social interaction with this creature.

Feared.Name: Fear
Feared.Description: This creature is in a state of panicked fear of something or someone. It can't voluntarily move closer to the source of this status effect, and suffers disadvantage on all rolls while it can see, hear, or otherwise perceive the source.

Petrified.Name: Petrified
Petrified.Description: This creature has been petrified. While this status effect applies, this creature and everything it's carrying turns to magical stone. While petrified, its weight increases tenfold and it stops aging. It is completely immobile, can't speak, and perceives nothing of its surroundings. It is immune to Poison damage and Poisoning; if it was already poisoned before this status effect took effect, the poisoning isn't cured, only paused. Should this creature be forced to make Strength, Dexterity, sight-based Perception, or Charisma checks, they automatically fail (this doesn't count as a critical failure). This creature takes halved damage from all sources except Aether, Earth, and Blunt damage while petrified, and attacks against it are always made with advantage.

Blind.Name: Blind
Blind.Description: This creature is blind in at least one eye. If blind in only one eye, it has disadvantage on Perception checks and attack rolls. If completely blind, sight-based Perception checks and ranged attacks automatically fail; melee attacks still only have disadvantage.

Concentration.Name: Concentration
Concentration.Description: This creature is concentrating on a task. If it takes damage, it must pass a Concentration check (1d20 + Constitution modifier + Concentration skill level) against a DC of (damage / 2, minimum 5), or its concentration breaks (this status effect is removed). Multiple "damage at the start of the turn" sources are summed together and checked only once per round.

Concealed.Name: Concealed
Concealed.Description: This creature is concealed/hidden in combat. While active, it generates Stealth's own pending FP (if configured) at the start of each of its own Combat turns.

Models.Name: Name
Models.AttributeOverrideHint: This weapon's Angriffswurf (attack roll) attribute bonus normally draws from its Model's own Attribute Modifiers Used. Enable this for a unique variant of that Model that should use different attributes instead.
Models.DamageTypeOverrideHint: This weapon's damage type (for Resistance/Weakness/Immunity/Absorption purposes) normally draws from its Model's own Damage Type. Enable this for a unique variant of that Model that should deal a different damage type instead.
Models.DurabilityMultiplierOverrideHint: This item's max Durability normally multiplies its Material's own base value by its Model's own Durability Multiplier (always 1 for items with no Model). Enable this to override that multiplier for this specific item instead.
Models.QualityHint: 100 = normal. Multiplicatively scales (rounded down) this item's own combined Material+Model flat attack/damage bonus (Weapon) or AC/MR bonus (Armor) - the wielder's own skill/attribute/Lehren contributions are never affected.

Heavy.Name: Heavy
Heavy.Hint: This item is heavy and requires a Strength score of at least the given requirement to use effectively. A weapon with this modifier can't be wielded in both hands until the character's Strength is well above that requirement.

Demanding.Name: Demanding
Demanding.Hint: This item is hard to handle and requires a Dexterity score of at least the given requirement to use effectively. A weapon with this modifier can't be wielded in both hands until the character's Dexterity is well above that requirement.

Draining.Name: Draining
Draining.Hint: Using this item quickly tires its bearer and requires a Constitution score of at least the given requirement to use effectively. A weapon with this modifier can't be wielded in both hands until the character's Constitution is well above that requirement.

Refined.Name: Refined
Refined.Hint: This weapon uses one of its listed attributes (user's choice). Incompatible with Specialized and Masterful.

Specialized.Name: Specialized
Specialized.Hint: This weapon uses its listed attribute twice. Incompatible with Simple, Refined and Masterful. If combined with the Two-Handed modifier, this modifier loses its effect unless the weapon is wielded two-handed.

Masterful.Name: Masterful
Masterful.Hint: This item is far better in the hands of someone who has mastered two attributes. Such an item uses two attributes - the higher of the two is used, and if both are equal, both are used. Incompatible with Simple, Refined and Specialized.

Rending.Name: Rending
Rending.Hint: A weapon with this modifier deals double damage to buildings, constructs, corporeal undead, objects, and inorganic obstacles.

Stunning.Name: Stunning
Stunning.Hint: A critical hit with a weapon with this modifier grants the target several stacks of Dazed. The amount equals Material Bonus / 2, multiplied by 1.5 / 2 / 2.5 if this weapon has the Heavy (Reduced) / Heavy / Heavy (Increased) modifier.

Disarming.Name: Disarming
Disarming.Hint: A creature using an item with this modifier can, as a reaction to a weapon attack, attempt to disarm the attacker. The attacker must succeed a DC 16 Dexterity or DC 18 Strength save (attacker's choice) or be disarmed on failure. The target's attack also fails on a failed save.

Ranged.Name: Ranged
Ranged.Hint: A weapon with this modifier can be used to attack at range (given in parentheses / disadvantage at extended range). In melee, i.e. 2m or less from the target, such a weapon can't be used to attack.

Reload.Name: Reload
Reload.Hint: After a weapon with this modifier has been used for Magazine Size attack rolls (Magazine Size 1 if unset), it must be reloaded before it can attack again. Pressing the weapon attack button again instead reloads it for the given Action Points, without attacking.

Flexible.Name: Flexible
Flexible.Hint: A weapon with this modifier can be used either one-handed or two-handed.

Shapeshifting.Name: Shapeshifting
Shapeshifting.Hint: This item can change its shape. It can turn a weapon into another one, or even into a piece of armor. This modifier can't change the item's overall mass. Costs 3 Action Points.

Infusion.Name: Infusion
Infusion.Hint: This weapon can be charged with mana, enabling the Magical Attacks and Deadly Attacks abilities. If this effect is natural to a material, it's lost if the weapon is enchanted (unless with this modifier). Antimagic items with this modifier can be enchanted or magically enhanced.

Unstable.Name: Unstable
Unstable.Hint: An item with this modifier is unstable. Each round, a D10 must be rolled - on a 10, the item spontaneously changes shape. This modifier can only be applied to items with the Shapeshifting modifier or the Shape-Adapting enchantment.

Long.Name: Long
Long.Hint: A weapon with this modifier has double the melee reach.

Light.Name: Light
Light.Hint: A weapon with this modifier grants its bearer an additional AP.

Antimagic.Name: Antimagic
Antimagic.Hint: An item with this modifier can't be enchanted, deals double damage to magical shields, and makes an illusion flicker on touch. The attacked creature also has disadvantage on its Concentration save. Armor made from materials with this modifier grants Magic Resistance equal to (AC granted / 2, rounded down).

Reach.Name: Reach
Reach.Hint: A weapon with this modifier can be used to attack at range (given in parentheses). Beyond 2m, the attack and damage roll use the given attribute modifier.

GiantSlayer.Name: Giant Slayer
GiantSlayer.Hint: Large-sized creatures take 25% extra damage, Gigantic-sized creatures take 50% extra damage, Titanic-sized creatures take 100% extra damage.

VeryLong.Name: Very Long
VeryLong.Hint: A weapon with this modifier has triple the melee reach.

Simple.Name: Simple
Simple.Hint: A weapon or armor with this modifier can be used effectively even without the corresponding skill. At the same time, it gains no bonus from skills (though skill points for the corresponding skill can still be earned). Incompatible with Specialized, Masterful and Refined.

Redirection.Name: Redirection
Redirection.Hint: The bearer of an item with this modifier can, as a reaction, redirect a non-area attack to the nearest creature within 2m, unless that creature succeeds a DC 15 Constitution save. Magical attacks can only be redirected with this modifier if it was granted via enchantment.

Silvered.Name: Silvered
Silvered.Hint: Weapons made from this material deal extra damage to certain creatures.

Concealed.Name: Concealed
Concealed.Hint: An attack with this weapon doesn't automatically break stealth. Creatures hit by an attack with such a weapon gain advantage on their next Observation check to reveal the attacker.

Wounding.Name: Wounding
Wounding.Hint: A successful attack with this weapon automatically inflicts a Wound.

Throwable.Name: Throwable
Throwable.Hint: This item can be thrown (no penalty on weapon attacks). A weapon enchanted with this modifier returns after the attack.

Shattering.Name: Shattering
Shattering.Hint: The AC of a creature hit by a weapon with this modifier is reduced for one round by the number of weapon dice. This effect can stack until the equipment's AC modifier reaches 0.

TwoHanded.Name: Two-Handed
TwoHanded.Hint: A weapon with this modifier must be wielded two-handed. Unless such a weapon also has the Heavy, Demanding or Draining modifier, it can be wielded one-handed if the bearer has a Strength score of 18 or higher.

Deployable.Name: Deployable
Deployable.Hint: A shield with this modifier can be deployed, after which it counts as an inorganic obstacle providing full or half cover.

ArmBound.Name: Arm-Bound
ArmBound.Hint: A shield with this modifier can't be lost unless the bearing arm is severed. Additionally, the hand of the arm wielding this shield can still be used for attacks.

Hardened.Name: Hardened (X)
Hardened.Hint: This item is hardened and grants AC increased by X (maximum is Material Bonus / 2).

Loud.Name: Loud
Loud.Hint: The bearer has disadvantage on Stealth checks while wearing this item.

Reflective.Name: Reflective
Reflective.Hint: Reflects 10% of the magical damage its bearer takes back onto the source.

Flawless.Name: Flawless
Flawless.Hint: A critical attack roll made against the bearer of an item with this modifier still hits automatically, but deals no extra damage.

Spiky.Name: Spiky
Spiky.Hint: Creatures that attack the bearer of such an item with a melee weapon attack take 1d6 piercing damage.

ItemSheet.ManaCoreFpGrantHint: Flat FP granted to the Manakern skill each time this is used - a designer-set value on this item itself, not a GM-configured rate.
ItemSheet.AllowBelowOneHint: This entry's flat reduction can push the cost below 1 (down to 0).
ItemSheet.ChargesDepleted: {actor} uses 1 charge. All of this item's charges are used up.
